newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks extend spirited rally.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks extend spirited rally.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks bucked a weak bond market to extend their spirited rally Tuesday amid renewed enthusiasm for stocks.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 27.29 points at 7,241.78 after Monday's jump of 142 points to a record finish of 7,214.49.
In the broader market, advancing issues beat declines by a small margin on heavy volume of 363 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond was off 4/32, which raised its yield to 6.89 percent from 6.88 percent on Monday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
The Nasdaq Composite Index was off 7.26 points to 1,331.98.
Analysts said the market had entered a phase in which investors believed they were in the best of all possible worlds and fears of interest rate tightening were receding.
"I guess euphoria rules. Everyone is interpreting news as bullish," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.

"The thesis now is that if the Federal Reserve raises interest rates it will extend the business cycle, and that is wonderful," he said. "If the Fed doesn't raise rates it means that it is content that the economy is slowing down, and that's perceived as wonderful too."
The upturn in blue-chips comes after a broad-based rally, which propelled the Dow a stunning 332 points higher last week.
"I'm not surprised that we are having rally. I've been in the bull camp. What is surprising is the magnitude of the rally," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross.

"Everyone became very bearish when the market was making its lows," he said. "They had raised a bit of cash and were concerned about stock prices going lower. So they did an about face, and what we got was a buying panic."
Blumberg said the market was due for a pause.

"I would say that, obviously, we need some rest," he said. "But everyone is so afraid of missing a rally that people keep trying to find some stock that will go up. They are afraid to own their favourite high techs and are trying to find issues which have lagged a bit."

Philip Morris Cos., the most actively traded NYSE issue, was down 1-1/4 at 42-3/4 while RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp. lost 1-1/2 at 31-1/8. The stocks soared Monday after a Florida jury ruled RJR's R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co. unit was not negligent in the death of a former smoker.
